blocks.text: Synthetic test record: the staff notes and sample describe a fictional employee test and a fictional buyer. They are not an actual Kesko project, meeting or agreement. Nothing below claims that Velho has met, spoken with or agreed anything with Kesko.

Kesko is a Finnish trade group with €12.5bn net sales in 2025, active in grocery, building and technical trade, and car trade. It has just agreed to buy Dahl's technical trade operations in Sweden, Norway and Denmark, with completion targeted for end-2026, and is planning a rights issue to fund part of it. The public signals suggest integration, cost discipline and warehouse modernisation are live topics. Velho's angle is to ask where manual order, invoice or data work slows teams down, and to test a small, bounded fix before anything bigger.

items.text: Kesko agreed to acquire Dahl's technical trade operations in Sweden, Norway and Denmark from Saint-Gobain, debt-free price €1.2bn, completion targeted by end-2026.
Kesko plans a €500-700m rights issue to refinance part of the bridge financing; EGM on 2026-10-30. Terms not yet set.
Manhattan Associates announced Kesko selected its ActiveWarehouse cloud warehouse solution, with an initial rollout covering five distribution centres.
Q2 2026 comparable operating profit rose to €194m; full-year 2026 guidance narrowed to €670-730m.
Kesko's stated goal is Group net sales of some €20 billion in the early 2030s.

blocks.text: Inferred, not confirmed: integrating Dahl, which keeps separate brands and units, may require manual reconciliation of order and financial data. No Kesko job ads for manual order or invoice roles were found.

items.text: As the Dahl integration approaches, which order, invoice or reporting steps still need someone to copy data between systems?
Where has the Manhattan warehouse rollout exposed workflow gaps that sit outside the core system?
If a small, bounded pilot could be run on one process, which process would your team most want tested first?
